articles.title: Essendon outline plan for James Hird after opting for Mark McVeigh as head coach
articles.summary: Hird can bring ‘significant value’ to club, says Bombers president. McVeigh takes on head coach role after leaving Sydney Swans. Essendon president Andrew Welsh and new coach Mark McVeigh have offered an olive branch to James Hird, declaring they intend to speak with the club great about a role at…
body: McVeigh was appointed Essendon coach on Monday, with the club opting for the Sydney Swans assistant ahead of fellow former Bombers player Hird, Fremantle’s Jaymie Graham and Adelaide’s Murray Davis.
Hird, who quit as Essendon coach in 2015 after a tenure marred by the club’s supplements saga, had pitched for the top job.
“I feel there is significant value James can bring,” Welsh said of Hird on Tuesday. “Not just tokenistic, but real value James can bring to our club and playing group.”

Hird didn’t answer Welsh’s calls, and the Essendon president sent him a text and hoped to speak with his former teammate on Tuesday. Hird was an assistant to McVeigh when he was interim GWS senior coach in 2022.

articles.title: Glaring weakness in goal remains but early signs Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea should be fun | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: The failure to replace Robert Sánchez remains a mystery but the new-look front three should buy time for the new manager’s principles to bed in. After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws, there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for…
body: They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left.

It could easily have gone wrong: in the final quarter-hour; Antonee Robinson lofted an effort wide with Robert Sánchez off his line and Ryan Sessegnon smacked a shot from a narrow angle straight at the Spanish keeper. But neither opportunity was taken and so Chelsea got Xabi Alonso’s reign off to a winning start.

At this stage, performances and learning the system are probably the most important thing, but if there is to be some sort of dart at the title, results matter if only to keep Chelsea somewhere near the race until the point at which Alonso’s principles are absorbed and they do find something close to top form.

articles.title: Enes Kanter reveals Natasha Cloud’s Sophie Cunningham comment before he was removed from game
articles.summary: Former NBA center Enes Kanter explained his perspective on what happened between him and Natasha Cloud during the Chicago Sky’s game against the Indiana Fever. Kanter made a huge show of attending the Sky vs.
body: Cloud aimed trash talk toward Kanter after a layup, while Kanter egged the 34-year-old Sky guard by standing up and spreading his arms, leading to his removal.
Kanter appeared on Fox News to discuss what happened between him and Cloud at the Sky game, with Kanter claiming Cloud made a Sophie Cunningham-related comment.

“The next possession, she came back and started yelling at me, ‘She is not going to sleep with you.’ Sophie Cunningham is not gonna sleep with me. I’m not trying to sleep with Sophie Cunningham; I want to make it very clear. Definitely not.”
Cunningham did have a 10-minute cameo in this game and is considered one of the main reasons that people like Kanter started paying attention to the WNBA over the trans athletes debate.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest close in on signing Liam Delap from Chelsea
articles.summary: Oliver Glasner wants two more buys in transfer window. Aston Villa target Club Brugge defender Joel Ordóñez. Nottingham Forest are in advanced talks with Chelsea over a deal for Liam Delap. Oliver Glasner wants two more signings before the transfer window closes a week on Tuesday.
body: Delap, who was on Forest’s radar when the striker opted to join Chelsea from Ipswich, is out of favour at Stamford Bridge and has been training away from Xabi Alonso’s first team. The 23-year-old was left out of Chelsea’s squad for their game at Fulham on Monday.

Glasner, who has implemented a three-man defence at Forest, is also keen to strengthen at wing-back. “The club is working very hard to get these deals done,” the Austrian head coach said. “I’m very confident that we will get in two more high-quality players.”

Forest have signed Ousmane Diomande, Xaver Schlager and Steven Benda this summer, paying a fee only for the former. Diomande joined in a £34m deal from Sporting. Forest host Leeds in the Carabao Cup second round on Tuesday, a rematch of their Premier League defeat last Saturday. Morgan Gibbs-White will miss the game because of a knee problem but Forest hope he will available for the trip to Liverpool on Saturday.

articles.title: Chelsea’s front three dazzle as they edge out Fulham in derby thriller
articles.summary: Perhaps there will come a time when Xabi Alonso has taught Chelsea how to master the art of game management. This is a team still to learn how to grind. Equally it is a team capable of hurting anyone, and although Alonso’s first outing as Chelsea’s manager featured plenty of terrible defending it…
body: No wonder Maxence Lacroix wanted to join in the fun. The £52m centre‑back marked his debut with a thrilling assist, storming forward to make Rogers’s first goal since his £117m move from Aston Villa. João Pedro was no less effective as the No 9, while the biggest positive for Alonso had to be Palmer looking rested, dangerous and determined to prove a point after his injury woes last season led to him being left out of England’s World Cup squad.

Keep playing this well and Thomas Tuchel will surely name Palmer alongside Rogers for the Nations League games next month. Chelsea’s two No 10s both got to do the “ice cold” celebration and their combinations with João Pedro should have been enough to ensure this 3-2 win against Fulham was less stressful.

There were reminders that Chelsea have much to improve if they want to challenge for the title. Their defending left much to be desired, even with the towering Lacroix in the middle of the back three, and Robert Sánchez’s feeble attempt to stop Josh King from scoring Fulham’s first goal bolsters the argument that Chelsea need a new No 1.

articles.title: UFC Sacramento Fight Night Weights Revealed
articles.summary: The UFC Sacramento fight night weights have been revealed by the California State Athletic Commission following the event. UFC Sacramento took place on Saturday, August 22, at Golden 1 Center in California’s state capital. The event was sanctioned by the CSAC.
body: In addition to revealing what the fighter payouts were to all 26 athletes on the card, the CSAC also revealed the fight night weights of all the fighters who competed, meaning the weight they actually fought at on the night of the fight, not what they weighed in the day before at the official UFC Sacramento weigh-ins.
Here is the full list of the UFC Sacramento fight night weights, via MMAFighting.com.

The biggest weight gainer from the official weigh-ins to fight day was UFC featherweight prospect Marcio Barbosa, who weighed in at 171 lbs, up from 145.5 lbs the day before, for a total gain of 25.5 lbs. His opponent, Ryan Kuse, weighed in at just 153.2 lbs on fight day, meaning Barbosa had a 17.8 lbs advantage in the cage.

In the main event, UFC middleweight contender Gregory Rodrigues put on 19.4 lbs, going from 185 at the weigh-ins to 204.4 lbs in the cage. His opponent, Anthony Hernandez, went from 186 lbs on weigh-in day to 202.2 lbs the next day, a 16.2 lbs difference.

articles.title: Linda Cohn Has a New Found Freedom After 34 Years With ESPN
articles.summary: "People are very busy, but they still want to hear what I have to say. Just like I was a part of their lives growing up watching on SportsCenter, they have welcomed me into their homes in this next chapter in the same way. That’s very gratifying to me."
body: After 34 years and more than 5,500 episodes anchoring sports television’s longest-running program, SportsCenter, Linda Cohn decided it was time for something different. Earlier this year, Cohn was celebrated in a daylong presentation during her return to Bristol, Connecticut. Memories, tributes and a highlight package or two were included, all with a focus on the impact and legacy Cohn left on so many over her three decades of service to the network.

In the days that followed, Cohn got right back to work. The project wasn’t another network or a return to her earlier days in radio. Instead, the National Sports Media Hall of Famer launched a YouTube channel dedicated to providing content that embraced the newfound freedom she gained by leaving the halls of the worldwide leader.

“The stuff that I have strong opinions on is the stuff I haven’t been allowed to say,” said Cohn. “The stuff that’s usually trending and hot topics are the things I tend to want to discuss the most. That’s the stuff that I had the gag order on every year I was with ESPN and weren’t allowed to talk about.”

Just like I was a part of their lives growing up watching on SportsCenter, they have welcomed me into their homes in this next chapter in the same way.

articles.title: Watson among Britons through in US Open qualifying
articles.summary: Heather Watson is among the British winners in the first round of US Open qualifying as she bids for a first New York main-drawn appearance in five years.
body: Britain's Heather Watson battled back from a set down against Claire Liu to keep alive her hopes of securing a first US Open main-draw appearance in five years.
The 34-year-old Watson beat sixth seed Liu 4-6 6-2 6-4 in the first round of qualifying in New York.
Watson almost let a double-break lead slip in the final set but held firm to set up a meeting with Spain's Angela Fita Boluda.
Toby Samuel, Jacob Fearnley, Billy Harris and Harry Wendelken all progressed in men's qualifying.

articles.title: Punishment that sends shiver down whole England team needed - Vaughan
articles.summary: A punishment to “send a shiver down the whole team” may be needed after Brydon Carse became the latest England cricketer involved in a drinking controversy, according to Michael Vaughan.
body: Pace bowler Carse was briefly placed under arrest on a night out with his Durham team-mates in Derby at the weekend.
The incident is being investigated by the Cricket Regulator and, as a result, Carse has been removed from the England squad for the second Test against Pakistan at Lord's on Thursday.

"Someone is going to have to get a punishment that sends a shiver down the whole England cricket team and right down through the programme, so that everyone knows that if you misbehave or bring any kind of bad reputation on to this team, you know what's going to come," former England captain Vaughan told BBC Radio 5 Live.
In October, England white-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer outside a nightclub in Wellington, New Zealand, with team-mates Jacob Bethell and Josh Tongue also present.

articles.title: Chelsea's electric front three edge out Fulham in pulsating MNF opener
articles.summary: Cole Palmer was back to his best to get Xabi Alonso's Chelsea career off to a winning start in a chaotic 3-2 victory at Fulham on Monday Night Football.
body: The Blues' attacking trio of Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers looked every bit the most potent in the Premier League as all three scored in a game where entertainment reigned and defending was an afterthought.

Palmer, finally injury-free and all the better for a summer off from England's World Cup campaign, scored one and made another in the kind of performance he had found so difficult to reproduce last season.
If his confidence on the pitch was not evidence enough, his response when Sky Sports asked how ready he was for the new season was emphatic. "Did you not watch the game?"
It took just 31 seconds for him to lay down a marker by teeing up an opener for Joao Pedro - himself refreshed after his surprise Brazil omission. The front three never looked back from there.

articles.title: All you need to know about the 2026 Solheim Cup
articles.summary: Where and when will the next Solheim Cup take place? How does the scoring system work? Which players can qualify? All you need to know about the 2026 edition...
body: The Solheim Cup is a three-day competition played between teams of 12 players from the USA and Europe.
The event launched in 1990 and was named in honour of Karsten and Louise Solheim and family - the founders of Karsten Manufacturing Corporation, which makes PING golf equipment.
The biggest team tournament in women's golf, where Team USA face Team Europe, is next held from September 11-13, 2026.
The Solheim Cup is back to even-numbered years to avoid clashing with the Ryder Cup, which moved to odd-numbered years after being postponed in 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

articles.title: Ex-Oregon State RB Anthony Hankerson Set For College Return After Being Waived By Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again. Hankerson signed with the Seahawks last week and rushed for 10 yards on five carries in their 19-16 preseason loss at Tennessee on Sunday night. He also caught two passes for nine yards.
body: He is among 16 players who graduated high school in 2022 and became eligible to play a fifth collegiate season thanks to a Louisiana court order last week. Once he clears waivers, he could enter the transfer portal.

Running back T.J. Harden, who played for the Seahawks in their preseason game against Dallas, was also among those granted a temporary restraining order by the Louisiana judge. Harden, who played last year at SMU and went undrafted, was waived by the Seahawks and entered the portal last week.
Hankerson was an undrafted rookie out of Oregon State who signed with Miami in April, then was waived earlier this month.
He ran for 1,086 yards and nine touchdowns last season, his second in Corvallis. He also had 22 catches for 123 yards.
